title: git clean: delete untracked files without deleting your work
summary: Build artefacts and stray files are cluttering status. Clean them out — and learn the dry-run habit that stops this command from eating a config file you needed.
mental_model: clean deletes files git is not tracking. It never touches tracked files, so it cannot destroy committed work — but untracked does not mean unimportant, and there is no undo.
danger: `git clean -xfd` deletes ignored files too: local .env files, virtualenvs, editor settings, downloaded fixtures. Always run `-n` first and read the list.

steps.title: Separate the three kinds of file
steps.why: app.py is tracked and modified. scratch.txt and build/ are untracked. debug.log and .env are ignored. clean treats all three differently, and status hides the third by default.

steps.title: Dry run first — always
steps.why: `-n` prints what would be deleted and touches nothing. Making this reflexive is the difference between a tidy repo and losing an afternoon of local config.
steps.expect: scratch.txt only — untracked directories need another flag.

steps.title: Include directories in the preview
steps.why: By default clean refuses to descend into untracked directories. `-d` includes them. Notice the preview now lists build/ as a whole.

steps.title: See what -x would take with it
steps.why: `-x` adds ignored files to the list: your .env and the logs. This is the flag that turns a tidy-up into an incident, so read this preview character by character.
steps.expect: scratch.txt, build/, debug.log and .env — including the one you would regret.

steps.title: Delete only what you meant to
steps.why: Run it without `-x` so ignored files survive, and confirm afterwards. Tracked modifications to app.py are untouched — clean has no opinion about tracked files.

verify.label: the ignored .env survived, because you left -x off

steps.title: Confirm your real work survived
steps.why: app.py is still modified and still yours. This is the reassuring half of clean: it operates strictly outside tracked content.

verify.label: untracked files and directories were removed
verify.hint: git clean -fd — the d is what removes directories

verify.label: .env survived, because -x was not used
verify.hint: adding -x would have deleted your local environment file

verify.label: the tracked modification was never at risk
app.py is still modified and still uncommitted

pitfalls: clean has no undo and untracked files are not in the object database. `-n` first, every time.
`-f` is mandatory by default (`clean.requireForce`), which is git protecting you from a typo.
`git clean -xfd` before a build is a genuinely useful reset — just never run it in a directory holding local secrets or data.
`git clean -i` gives an interactive picker if you want some of the list but not all of it.
cheatsheet: dry run: what would be deleted
…including ignored files — read this one carefully
also delete ignored files: a true blank slate
